findings.title: User OAuth2 authorization code flow for personal accounts
findings.detail: Todoist documents third-party applications obtaining a user-authorized API token through OAuth2. The flow uses an authorization request, then a token exchange at the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and code.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own Todoist account.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels and filters. It is the least-privilege documented grant for listing active task titles and does not permit creating, updating, completing or deleting tasks.

steps.title: Send user to Todoist consent screen with read-only scope and check callback
steps.detail: Redirect the customer's browser to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, scope=data:read, a random state and response_type=code. The customer approves in the browser; the app verifies the returned state matches before using the code. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: Callback arrives at the configured redirect_uri with a code and the same state value that was sent.

evidence.quote: An example of the URL to the authorization endpoint:
task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

fields: client_id: from registered app
scope: data:read (read-only task access)
state: random value generated by the app
response_type: code

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code returned to the redirect URL for an access token at the documented token endpoint. Authenticate with client_id and client_secret in the POST body (client_secret_post). Not executed; uses the code from the consent step.
steps.doneWhen: Response is HTTP 200 JSON containing access_token and token_type Bearer; refresh_token and expires_in are present when refresh tokens are enabled.

evidence.quote: $ curl "https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token" \

code The code that was sent in the query string to the redirect URL in the previous step.

fields: client_id: from registered app
client_secret: from registered app
code: from redirect query string after consent
redirect_uri: must match the registered redirect URL

steps.title: Read first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the customer's Bearer access token and limit=50 to read active task titles from the content field of each result. The customer's own account is used; no resource ID is required. Expected output: HTTP 200 with a results array and next_cursor.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 response with results array; each result's content property is captured as a task title; next_cursor is recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for get /api/v1/tasks: $.results (array)
Response JSON paths for get /api/v1/tasks: $.results[].content (string)
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

fields: Authorization: Bearer token from exchange step
limit: 50 (documented default and maximum 200)

steps.title: Confirm read-only boundary with a documented exclusion check
steps.detail: Confirm the read-only boundary without relying on a successful read to prove write denial. Use only GET to fetch one active task by ID from the customer's own results in the prior list step; this confirms read access only. Write denial is established by the data:read grant itself (read-only access to tasks, projects, labels and filters, which excludes create, update, complete and delete) and by inspecting the outgoing request log to verify that no POST, DELETE or other write method was sent. Do not call any create, update, complete, move, reopen or delete endpoint to test this.
steps.doneWhen: GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} returns HTTP 200 for a task from the customer's own list, the token's granted scope is confirmed as data:read, and the outgoing request log shows only GET requests.

Returns a single active (non-completed) task by ID

steps.title: Read continuation page of active tasks until next_cursor is null
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with the same limit and the cursor value from the prior response's next_cursor, passing the cursor as-is. Repeat until next_cursor is null, which is the documented end of results. Do not invent or decode cursors. Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor set to the prior next_cursor and the same limit, until the response's next_cursor is null. This is the documented end condition for this endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: Requests continue with cursor until next_cursor is null; all result pages are collected. A response returns next_cursor null, confirming the end of results; all task titles across pages are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
